title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
AI-generated synthetic media enabled large-scale impersonation of a real person to commit fraud. Scammers created fake videos and social media profiles using AI to pose as an established immigration attorney, then solicited payment from vulnerable immigrants for fraudulent legal services. The deployment failure was the absence of identity verification on social media platforms, which allowed thousands of impersonation accounts to operate simultaneously across multiple services.

The scam targeted immigrants seeking legal assistance, a population at particular risk of financial harm and exploitation. Victims were directed through messaging apps where they could not verify they were communicating with a licensed attorney. What would have caught this: platform verification systems that confirm professional credentials before allowing someone to offer legal services, or human review of accounts claiming professional authority before they accumulate followers.

It is not established whether the AI systems used were designed or marketed for impersonation, or whether the social media platforms deployed detection systems that failed to identify the accounts.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the victim of a widespread identity theft scheme. Criminals are using artificial intelligence to create fake videos and social media profiles that impersonate him, offering fraudulent immigration services to vulnerable immigrants. The scammers promise services like US residency assistance for undocumented immigrants in exchange for thousands of dollars, often requesting payment through apps like Venmo and Zelle. Leal discovered the fraud when potential clients began calling his office, and the situation has escalated dramatically over the past three months.

An anti-piracy company hired by Leal's firm has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake accounts across social media platforms, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram. The scams typically direct victims to contact a phone number via WhatsApp, where fraudsters send phony contracts and fake testimonials from supposed clients. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the scheme. He warns immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online and to avoid paying for immigration services through mobile payment applications.
